editorial.headline: LPG Cylinder Retail: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers retail sales of cooking LPG cylinders, including specified LPG sub-bases and bases—open nationally to foreign ownership, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47772 covers the retail sale of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) in cylinders for cooking. Its scope explicitly includes specified LPG sub-bases and LPG bases, placing the activity in the practical, consumer-facing trade of bottled cooking gas rather than in a broader description of energy commerce. The definition is narrow in a useful way: the registered activity is the retailing of LPG cylinders for household cooking use.

The activity is available across the full scale range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In other words, the national position permits full foreign ownership for this activity. That openness is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021; there is no lower foreign-share cap stated in the record.

Bali presents a materially different registration outcome. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The Bali status is blocked due to risk class because, at the Besar scale, every scope is classified as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah in OSS risk terms. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities from PMA registration. The restriction is therefore not a national foreign-ownership limit: it is a Bali-specific bar on PMA registration arising from the activity’s recorded risk classification.

For founders, the distinction deserves to be held plainly. Nationally, KBLI 47772 is open and can carry foreign ownership up to 100%. In Bali, that national opening does not translate into a PMA registration route for this activity. The relevant question is not whether foreign ownership is permitted in Indonesia in the abstract, but whether the Bali moratorium permits PMA registration for this particular risk-class outcome. On the record provided, it does not.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 47772 is open to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, it cannot be registered as PMA.
